message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the same ancestor that gave rise to all placental mammals (Eutheria).  
That ancestor lived roughly 100 – 110 million years ago, before the major lineages that would become the carnivores (like lions) and the odd‑toed ungulates (like zebras) split off from one another.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want a biological answer. The lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) are both mammals, but belong to different orders: lions are Carnivora, zebras are Perissodactyla. Their common ancestor would be at the level of the last common ancestor of all placental mammals? Actually, lion and zebra diverged earlier. The last common ancestor of all placental mammals is the ancestor of the group Eutheria. But maybe they want the last common ancestor of the two species: the last common ancestor of the family Felidae and Equidae. That would be the ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the ancestor of the clade that includes all placental mammals except monotremes. So the last common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which lived about 100 million years ago. But if we want a more specific answer: the last common ancestor of the two species is the ancestor of the clade that includes the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the ancestor of the clade called "Eutheria" or "Placentalia". So the answer: the last common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which lived around 100 million years ago. Or we could say: the last common ancestor of the two species is the ancestor of the clade that includes the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the ancestor of the clade "Eutheria". So the answer: the last common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which lived about 100 million years ago. Alternatively, we can mention the last common ancestor of the two species is the ancestor of the clade "Carnivora + Perissodactyla" which is the ancestor of the clade "Eutheria". So the answer: the last common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which lived about 100 million years ago. Let's answer accordingly.
